# Sirach Chapter 28 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 28 | **Date:** 2026-03-17

---

**28:1** He who takes vengeance will receive vengeance from the LORD, and the LORD will keep firm account of his sins.

**28:2** Forgive your neighbor the wrong he has done, and then when you pray your sins will be forgiven.

**28:3** Does a man harbor anger against a man — and then seek healing from the LORD?

**28:4** He has no mercy on a man like himself — and he makes petition about his own sins?

**28:5** He, being flesh himself, holds wrath — who then will make atonement for his sins?

**28:6** Remember your last things and stop hating; remember corruption and death and abide by the commandments.

**28:7** Remember the commandments and do not be angry with your neighbor, and remember the covenant of the Most High and overlook offense.

**28:8** Keep away from strife and you will diminish your sins; for a hot-tempered man fans the flames of strife,

**28:9** and a sinful man troubles his friends and throws enmity among those who are at peace.

**28:10** According to the fuel of the fire, so it burns; and according to the stubbornness of a man, so the strife grows great; and according to his strength, so the anger burns the greater.

**28:11** A hasty quarrel kindles a fire, and a hasty dispute sheds blood.

**28:12** If you blow on a spark it blazes up; and if you spit on it, it goes out — and both come from your mouth.

**28:13** Curse the whisperer and the double-tongued man, for he has destroyed many who were at peace.

**28:14** The third tongue has shaken many loose and scattered them from nation to nation; it has destroyed fortified cities and overturned the houses of great men.

**28:15** The third tongue has driven capable wives away and deprived them of the fruit of their labors.

**28:16** Whoever heeds it will find no rest, and will not dwell in quietness.

**28:17** A blow from a whip raises a bruise, but a blow of the tongue shatters bones.

**28:18** Many have fallen by the edge of the sword, but not so many as have fallen because of the tongue.

**28:19** Blessed is the man who has been sheltered from it, who has not passed through its fury, who has not dragged its yoke or been bound in its chains.

**28:20** For its yoke is a yoke of iron and its chains are chains of bronze.

**28:21** The death it brings is an evil death, and Hades is preferable to it.

**28:22** It will have no power over the devout; they will not be burned in its flame.

**28:23** Those who forsake the LORD will fall into it, and it will burn in them and not be quenched; it will be unleashed against them like a lion and ravage them like a leopard.

**28:24** Fence your fields in with thorns; bind your silver and your gold securely.

**28:25** And make a door and a bolt for your mouth; and a balance and a scale for your words.

**28:26** Take care lest you stumble by means of it, lest you fall before one who lies in wait.
